results.name: MvPolynomial.mem_support_iff
results.source_text:
@[simp, grind =]
theorem mem_support_iff {p : MvPolynomial σ R} {m : σ →₀ ℕ} : m ∈ p.support ↔ p.coeff m ≠ 0 := by
  simp [support, coeff]

theorem supp_subset_range (h : natDegree p < m) : p.support ⊆ Finset.range m := fun _n hn =>
  mem_range.2 <| (le_natDegree_of_mem_supp _ hn).trans_lt h

results.name: Turing.TM0.Supports
results.source_text:
/-- The raw definition of a Turing machine does not require that
  `Γ` and `Λ` are finite, and in practice we will be interested
  in the infinite `Λ` case. We recover instead a notion of
  "effectively finite" Turing machines, which only make use of a
  finite subset of their states. We say that a set `S ⊆ Λ`
  supports a Turing machine `M` if `S` is closed under the
  transition function and contains the initial state. -/
def Supports (M : Machine Γ Λ) (S : Set Λ) :=
  default ∈ S ∧ ∀ {q a q' s}, (q', s) ∈ M q a → q ∈ S → q' ∈ S
results.docstring:
The raw definition of a Turing machine does not require that
`Γ` and `Λ` are finite, and in practice we will be interested
in the infinite `Λ` case. We recover instead a notion of
"effectively finite" Turing machines, which only make use of a
finite subset of their states. We say that a set `S ⊆ Λ`
supports a Turing machine `M` if `S` is closed under the
transition function and contains the initial state.

results.name: Turing.TM2.Supports
results.source_text:
/-- Given a TM2 machine `M` and a set `S` of states, `Supports M S` means that all states in
`S` jump only to other states in `S`. -/
def Supports (M : Λ → Stmt Γ Λ σ) (S : Finset Λ) :=
  default ∈ S ∧ ∀ q ∈ S, SupportsStmt S (M q)
results.docstring:
Given a TM2 machine `M` and a set `S` of states, `Supports M S` means that all states in
`S` jump only to other states in `S`.

results.name: MulAction.Supports
results.source_text:
/-- A set `s` supports `b` if `g • b = b` whenever `g • a = a` for all `a ∈ s`. -/
@[to_additive /-- A set `s` supports `b` if `g +ᵥ b = b` whenever `g +ᵥ a = a` for all `a ∈ s`. -/]
def Supports (s : Set α) (b : β) :=
  ∀ g : G, (∀ ⦃a⦄, a ∈ s → g • a = a) → g • b = b
results.docstring: A set `s` supports `b` if `g • b = b` whenever `g • a = a` for all `a ∈ s`.

results.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.support
results.source_text:
/-- A point `x` is in the support of `μ` if any open neighborhood of `x` has positive measure.
We provide the definition in terms of the filter-theoretic equivalent
`∃ᶠ u in (𝓝 x).smallSets, 0 < μ u`. -/
protected def support (μ : Measure X) : Set X := {x : X | ∃ᶠ u in (𝓝 x).smallSets, 0 < μ u}
results.docstring:
A point `x` is in the support of `μ` if any open neighborhood of `x` has positive measure.
We provide the definition in terms of the filter-theoretic equivalent
`∃ᶠ u in (𝓝 x).smallSets, 0 < μ u`.

results.name: Finsupp.toFinset_toMultiset
results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem toFinset_toMultiset [DecidableEq α] (f : α →₀ ℕ) : f.toMultiset.toFinset = f.support := by
  refine f.induction ?_ ?_
  · rw [toMultiset_zero, Multiset.toFinset_zero, support_zero]
  · intro a n f ha hn ih
    rw [toMultiset_add, Multiset.toFinset_add, ih, toMultiset_single, support_add_eq,
      support_single _ hn, Multiset.toFinset_nsmul _ _ hn, Multiset.toFinset_singleton]
    refine Disjoint.mono_left support_single_subset ?_
    rwa [Finset.disjoint_singleton_left]

results.name: Function.support
results.source_text:
@[to_additive /-- `support` of a function is the set of points `x` such that `f x ≠ 0`. -/]
def mulSupport (f : ι → M) : Set ι := {x | f x ≠ 1}
results.docstring: `support` of a function is the set of points `x` such that `f x ≠ 0`.

results.name: ZMod.val_natCast
results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem val_natCast (n a : ℕ) : (a : ZMod n).val = a % n := by
  cases n
  · rw [Nat.mod_zero]
    exact Int.natAbs_natCast a
  · apply Fin.val_natCast

results.name: ZMod.val
results.source_text:
/-- `val a` is a natural number defined as:
  - for `a : ZMod 0` it is the absolute value of `a`
  - for `a : ZMod n` with `0 < n` it is the least natural number in the equivalence class

See `ZMod.valMinAbs` for a variant that takes values in the integers.
-/
def val : ∀ {n : ℕ}, ZMod n → ℕ
  | 0 => Int.natAbs
  | n + 1 => ((↑) : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ)
results.docstring:
`val a` is a natural number defined as:
- for `a : ZMod 0` it is the absolute value of `a`
- for `a : ZMod n` with `0 < n` it is the least natural number in the equivalence class

See `ZMod.valMinAbs` for a variant that takes values in the integers.

results.name: ZMod.natCast_zmod_val
results.source_text:
/-- So-named because the coercion is `Nat.cast` into `ZMod`. For `Nat.cast` into an arbitrary ring,
see `ZMod.natCast_val`. -/
theorem natCast_zmod_val {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n) : (a.val : ZMod n) = a := by
  cases n
  · cases NeZero.ne 0 rfl
  · apply Fin.cast_val_eq_self
results.docstring:
So-named because the coercion is `Nat.cast` into `ZMod`. For `Nat.cast` into an arbitrary ring,
see `ZMod.natCast_val`.

results.name: Mathlib.Meta.NormNum.evalNatCast
results.source_text:
/-- The `norm_num` extension which identifies an expression `Nat.cast n`, returning `n`. -/
@[norm_num Nat.cast _, NatCast.natCast _] def evalNatCast : NormNumExt where eval {u α} e := do
  let sα ← inferAddMonoidWithOne α
  let .app n (a : Q(ℕ)) ← whnfR e | failure
  guard <|← withNewMCtxDepth <| isDefEq n q(Nat.cast (R := $α))
  let ⟨na, pa⟩ ← deriveNat a q(Nat.instAddMonoidWithOne)
  haveI' : $e =Q $a := ⟨⟩
  return .isNat sα na q(isNat_natCast $a $na $pa)
results.docstring: The `norm_num` extension which identifies an expression `Nat.cast n`, returning `n`.
